question: What is the main goal of the evaluation phase in patient care?

options.A: To collect initial baseline medical history
options.B: To write a new doctor prescription
options.C: To calculate daily hospital billing costs
options.D: To determine if patient goals were met

explanation: Evaluation checks whether the planned nursing interventions successfully met the expected patient outcomes. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why is evaluation considered an ongoing activity?

options.A: Doctors change medication schedules every shift
options.B: Patient conditions can change rapidly at any time
options.C: Patients prefer constant questioning by nurses
options.D: Hospital management requires hourly status updates

explanation: Because a patient's health status fluctuates, midwives continuously evaluate responses to care to keep interventions relevant and safe. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h1)

question: What do you compare actual patient outcomes against during evaluation?
explanation: Actual patient outcomes are measured directly against the specific goals and targets set during the planning phase of care. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h2)

question: A new mother was expected to successfully breastfeed within 24 hours, but her baby still struggles to latch. How is this classified?
explanation: Since the target was not reached within the specified timeframe, the goal is unmet and the care plan needs adjustment. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h2)

question: When should a midwife decide to modify a patient care plan?

options.A: Whenever a new nurse takes over the morning shift
options.B: When evaluation shows goals are consistently unmet
options.C: Only when the patient demands to leave the hospital
options.D: At the exact end of every single week of admission

explanation: Care plans are flexible tools that must be revised when evaluation proves current interventions are not producing the desired results. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which action is a direct part of modifying a care plan?

options.A: Transferring financial responsibility to the family
options.B: Deleting all previous nurse signatures from records
options.C: Discharging the patient without further review
options.D: Adjusting target timelines and nursing actions

explanation: Modifying a care plan involves changing diagnoses, updating timelines, or trying new interventions to better address patient needs. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is charting nursing care before it is actually performed strictly prohibited?

options.A: It makes the handwriting look untidy on the chart
options.B: It takes too much time during morning handover
options.C: It causes the hospital to run out of paper forms
options.D: It falsifies records and compromises patient safety

explanation: Charting care before it happens creates false legal records and can lead to missed interventions if emergencies distract the nurse. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following is an example of objective nursing documentation?

options.A: Labor room is extremely busy and noisy
options.B: Patient looks very happy and relaxed today
options.C: FHR is 140 beats per minute, regular rhythm
options.D: Mother seems anxious about her baby health

explanation: Objective documentation relies on measurable, observable facts rather than personal opinions or vague emotional interpretations. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h4)

question: What does the legal phrase 'if it was not charted, it was not done' mean for midwives?

options.A: Uncharted tasks do not require hospital supplies
options.B: Patients can refuse to pay if notes are short
options.C: Unrecorded care has no legal proof in court
options.D: Nurses only get paid for paperwork, not actions

explanation: In a legal dispute, courts rely strictly on written records; unrecorded care is legally considered never to have happened. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which situation represents a serious legal and ethical breach in nursing documentation?

options.A: Signing your full name after a procedure
options.B: Writing patient statements in quotation marks
options.C: Using black ink for all routine ward notes
options.D: Backdating an entry to cover up missed care

explanation: Altering timelines or backdating records to hide delayed or missed care is falsification and carries severe legal penalties. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h5)

question: A midwife gives oxytocin to manage postpartum hemorrhage. What is the correct sequence of clinical action?

options.A: Monitor uterine tone, then chart the findings immediately
options.B: Chart the medication first before assessing the patient
options.C: Ask a junior student nurse to document the procedure
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to record all events

explanation: Evaluate the clinical effect of an intervention first and then document those exact findings right away while details are fresh. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of clear documentation for shift handovers?

options.A: It eliminates the need for verbal communication entirely
options.B: It reduces the total number of working hours for staff
options.C: It ensures safe and continuous patient care between shifts
options.D: It allows doctors to avoid visiting patients in the morning

explanation: Accurate records provide incoming staff with reliable data, preventing gaps in patient care during shift changes. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T6#BMP120_U1_T6_h6)
